history.summary: RELATED to seq 1576 (Hateshwari Mata Temple, Hatkoti) - this is the smaller Shiva shrine standing ADJACENT to the Devi shrine within the same Hatkoti temple complex on the Pabbar river bank, not the same shrine. It is architecturally in the same Nagara stone style as the other Hatkoti temples and is reported to house a large Shivling - said to be bigger than the shrine's own doorway - with an intricately carved wooden ceiling showing figures of gods and goddesses. It shares the complex's facilities and festival calendar (kirtan ghar, dharamshala, yagyashala, Satsang Bhawan). CAUTION: sources almost never describe this shrine separately from the Hateshwari complex, so details specific to it are thin (verify). The complex photo used in media may show the main Devi shrine rather than the Shiva shrine itself.

town: Hatkoti (CSV town correct; village in Jubbal tehsil)
town_description: Hatkoti is a village in Jubbal tehsil of Shimla district, on the banks of the Pabbar river about 100-102 km from Shimla town. It sits at the meeting point of the Pabbar, Bishkulti and Raanvati streams, a confluence regarded as a pilgrimage spot in itself. The ancient temple complex here - Shiva and Shakti shrines in Nagara stone architecture - is the village's main draw; the Sawra Kuddu hydroelectric project (111 MW) is nearby.

travel.road: Drive from Shimla via Theog-Kotkhai-Jubbal-Hatkoti (~3-4 hours, ~100 km); 14 km from Rohru (verify).
